text:
mike.t: quick check — CinderHealth cutover tomorrow. Need to lock owners for egress rules + fallback routing. Who's taking network + who owns the fallback policy?

lina.k: I can own the egress rules. Will validate CIDR list and HA endpoints.

vijay: i'll take fallback policy (model variant <-> region mappings). will draft canary steps.

jordan: +1 to vijay for fallback. also, remind infra on proxy cert rotation window.

mike.t: thanks. lina, can you confirm whether we need to open 443 to 10.8.4.0/24 or to specific hosts? security asked for minimum scope.

lina.k: security asked for host-level whitelisting. current list from Cinder: 10.8.4.21, 10.8.4.22. i'll validate with them in the morning.

nora: @lina.k FYI the customer is air-gapped except for a transit host. they'll only allow egress via the transit node (10.8.4.11). we may need a NAT on their side.

lina.k: ok noted. i'll change plan: allow 10.8.4.11 outbound and update puppet rules. quick draft for infra runbook:
```
# allow outbound to model-store via transit
iptables -A OUTPUT -p tcp -d 10.8.4.11 --dport 443 -j ACCEPT
# block everything else to external model endpoints
iptables -A OUTPUT -p tcp --dport 443 -j DROP
```

vijay: that works. for fallback policy, i'm proposing: primary -> dedicated-rg-us, fallback -> hosted-micro-us (quantized). will put details in the PR.

mike.t: PR ping: mike.t/eng-runtime/PR#4234 still needs review (routing changes + tests). can someone from runtime glance? cc @jordan

jordan: will review tonight. main question: do we auto-fallback on 5xx or after token timeout?

vijay: prefer on 5xx + latency spike > 500ms for 3 consecutive requests. avoids noisy transient fails.

ops-bot: deploy-schedule: reminder — private-cutover-cinderhealth scheduled 2026-03-18T09:00Z. Maintenance window: 09:00-11:00Z.

mike.t: timeline check — lina, can you finish firewall PR + ops runbook by 07:00Z? vijay, have fallback policy + tests by 08:00Z? jordan, review by 21:00 local?

lina.k: will aim for 06:30Z. posting runbook link here when ready.

vijay: yes, i'll have tests and CI passing by 07:30Z.

jordan: review scheduled for 20:30 local, will push comments ASAP.

nora: i'll coordinate with the customer's network lead (Anya) to confirm transit NAT is in place. expecting a reply in the morning.

mike.t: blockers?

lina.k: one blocker: customer requires HSM-backed TLS client auth for the transit host. we currently rely on certs from their side; need to confirm whether we can accept client cert or they will rotate. Security wants a confirmation email.

jordan: code-level blocker: my last CI run flaked on the integration test that simulates a cutover under load — will re-run and report.

vijay: small ask: can we add a fallback metric tag (cutover_customer:cinderhealth) so we can filter SLO dashboards post-cutover?

mike.t: good call — ops, please add that tag to the canary pipeline.

ops-bot: note saved: metric_tag:cutover_customer=cinderhealth.

mike.t: perfect. if no objections, we'll proceed with the plan. final cadence: async updates here; escalate to #incidents if we see >5% error during canary. thanks all. :thumbsup:
